title: Potential applications of exoskeletons in the workplace for the secondary prevention
summary:
Demographic change has a significant impact on many companies. In the coming years, the number of older workers with reduced work capacity is expected to rise. Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) and musculoskeletal complaints (MSCs) play a particular role in this context and are closely linked with work-related physical strain such as lifting and carrying heavy loads or working in awkward positions. MSDs are one of the most common work-related health problems across all sectors within the European Union.
Over the past few years, the use of exoskeletons has been discussed as a potential means of preventing work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WRMSDs). An exoskeleton is a wearable device that provides mechanical support. As assistive systems exoskeletons promise specific relief for physically strained body parts, thereby opening up approaches to ergonomic work design.
The study examines the potential applications of exoskeletons in secondary prevention. 
We focus on employees with musculoskeletal complains who are able to work but still perform back-straining tasks.

interventions.name: The study on the potential applications of exoskeletons in the secondary prevention involves monitoring employees (n=8) with back-straining jobs and existing back problems as they test an exoskeleton.
